formats.key: DelegatedUserDecryptRequestVerification(bytes publicKey,address[] contractAddresses,address delegatorAddress,uint256 startTimestamp,uint256 durationDays,bytes extraData)
effects: The signer (the delegate) authorizes the Zama KMS to decrypt ciphertexts held by delegatorAddress in the listed contractAddresses, using the decryption rights the delegator gave the signer.
The decrypted values are re-encrypted to publicKey, so whoever holds the matching private key can read the delegator's confidential data.
The authorization is valid from startTimestamp for durationDays days.
extraData is passed to the decryption request as opaque context. No tokens, ETH or allowances move.
formats.shown: Authorize decryption on behalf of the delegator address, for the listed contracts, valid from a date for N days. The public key and extraData are hidden.

findings.title: DelegatedUserDecryptRequestVerification hides publicKey, the key whose holder can read the decrypted data.
findings.evidence: descriptor.json field {"path":"publicKey","label":"Public key","format":"raw","visible":"never"}. In Zama's flow the decryption result is re-encrypted to this key, so the signature lets that key's holder read the data. Case 0: publicKey 0x2000…0001 is not on the screen.
findings.fix: Nothing a person can check from a raw key. Wallets could compare it with a key the dApp generated locally. Keep it hidden, but say in the intent that the data is released to the requesting app's key.

findings.title: DelegatedUserDecryptRequestVerification hides extraData, which the screen cannot interpret.
findings.evidence: descriptor.json field {"path":"extraData","format":"raw","visible":"never"}. Case 0: extraData is 0x. It is opaque bytes that move no assets.
findings.fix: None needed while extraData stays empty. Show it if a version ever gives it meaning.

couldNotCheck: The verifying contract 1:0x0f6024a97684f7d90ddb0faad79cb15f2c888d24 is unverified: abi.json is null and there is no source. So I could not confirm the EIP-712 type string, the field order or the 'Decryption'/'1' domain, or what the contract does with the signature. A mismatch would make the signature valid for something other than what is shown.
